title.en: Reproduction: hands-on activities from the textbook

text.en: Plants make new plants from cuttings, yeast makes buds and flowers carry the parts of reproduction. Chapter 11 invites you to see each.

Activity 11.1 asks you to talk to gardeners and observe cutting, grafting and layering, three ways of vegetative propagation.
Activity 11.2 mixes yeast in sugar solution, keeps it warm for one or two hours and looks at a drop under a microscope, where buds on yeast cells show budding.
Activity 11.3 keeps a moist slice of bread or roti in a damp chamber to grow bread mould, showing reproduction by spores.
Activity 11.4 uses coloured beads for chromosomes to model how crossing over mixes characters, which explains variation.
Activity 11.5 collects flowers and records the floral parts from the outer whorl to the inner one in a table.
Activity 11.6 uses pea flowers. Remove the stamens from some buds and flowers, then compare seed formation, which shows the role of pollination.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma, within the same flower or between flowers of the same plant (self-pollination) or of different plants (cross-pollination).
Activity 11.7 compares pollen production and seed formation for different pollination strategies in a table.

problem.en: Name the three methods of vegetative propagation in Activity 11.1.

text.en: Cutting plants a piece of stem.
Grafting joins a shoot to a rooted plant.
Layering roots a bent branch while it is still attached.

prompt.en: What do the yeast and bread mould activities show?

points.en: Cutting, grafting and layering are vegetative propagation.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma.
